findings.reason: the write paths must gain `reckon/serve.py` (and the wake source must be reported from `wait`) or the generation state must be relocated, otherwise the node either blocks or lands cases (4) and (5) untested.
findings.text: §15 makes the change-stream handler's invalidation a relay that "keeps that report's generation" and requires that handler to distinguish a relayed detector report from a kernel report ("a change reported by another source after the pass makes the record untrusted"; cases (4) and (5)), but the handler's call site and the wake-source distinction both live in `reckon/serve.py` — the handler at `reckon/serve.py:2755-2860` calls `_invalidate_tree_views(docs_dir, changed_at=changed_at)` with no source and no generation, `_invalidate_tree_views` itself is defined at `reckon/serve.py:1443`, and its two wake sources are already collapsed to a bare boolean by `_ProjectChangeWatch.wait` (`reckon/change_streams.py:101-113`), while §15's Write paths name only `reckon/metadata_index.py`, `reckon/change_streams.py` and the test file — so a worker implementing the spec exactly cannot reach case (5)'s observable ("the change-stream read that follows a detector pass ... stats only the moved directory") without editing a file outside its grant, which the spec calls a blocker.

findings.reason: without naming that the taken identities feed `build_index`'s own loop, the node's named check fails for a cause outside the deliverable as written and the node must invent the seeding.
findings.text: §15's mechanism says the read "takes the identity of every other recorded directory from that pass instead of stat-ing it", but the read is `index_rows` → `_reuse_covered` → `_covered_files...`/`_build_and_cache` → `build_index`, and `build_index` re-derives an identity for every entry of the `dirs` map it is handed (`reckon/metadata_index.py:565-567`), so identities merely taken by `_reuse_covered` are stat-ed again by the build unless they are also seeded into the pass-scoped observation map `covered_dir_identity` reads (`reckon/metadata_index.py:168-188`); case (1)'s spy count is therefore N, not the one the case asserts, for a reason §15 never names.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor §15 names resolves: `_reuse_covered`, `covered_dir_identity` and `_dir_identity` at `reckon/metadata_index.py:395,168,879`; `_fast_tree`, `_slow_pass` and `reckon/serve.py:2805` in the change handler; §7's live pass and its comment at `reckon/serve.py` / plan comment `c-run-r-20261023T065110156872-the-cold-start-controls-redden-their-gates`; §13 and §14 both exist as sections.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §15's case (1) measures "the next `index_rows` read stats exactly the one moved directory" with a spy on `_dir_identity`, but the read re-stats every covered directory after `_reuse_covered` returns.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §15 puts every log "under the run directory with a revision header and ends in EXIT=", matching §13 and §14, and writes the gate on the fleet allocation rather than a login-node or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §15's symbols are mechanism-named (`_reuse_covered`, `_dir_identity`, `_fast_tree`), the only identifier it introduces is the test filename `tests/test_a_read_...py`, and no plan label, ticket or version tag reaches source.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §15 places its trust rule at the change-stream handler's call site in `reckon/serve.py`, a file its declared write paths do not include, and the two-wake-source distinction its cases (4) and (5) require is not available there.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 carries one deliverable (the read takes recorded-directory identities from the detector's pass), with its cases and live re-measure as evidence for that one measure.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §15 declares `depends-on: [the-page-paints-from-an-index#s14]` in `plan-section-depends-on` and §14 sits directly above it in the section list, which is the ordering §15's own text ("This runs after §14, which shares `reckon/metadata_index.py`") relies on.
